title: Modulation of anomalous Hall angle in a magnetic topological semimetal
authors: Jinying Yang, Yanxing Shang, Xingchen Liu, Yibo Wang, Xuebin Dong, Qingqi Zeng, Meng Lv, Shen Zhang, Yang Liu, Binbin Wang, Hongxiang Wei, Yizheng Wu, Stuart Parkin, Gangqin Liu, Claudia Felser, Enke Liu, Baogen Shen
abstract: The anomalous Hall angle (θA) is a measure of the efficiency of converting a longitudinal driving current to a transverse spin-polarized Hall current. For anomalous Hall sensing, a large anomalous Hall angle can improve the sensitivity of magnetic field detection. However, modulation of this angle is challenging and magnetic materials typically have low angles of 0.1 to 3°. Here, we report modulation of the anomalous Hall angle in the magnetic Weyl semimetal Co3Sn2S2. We propose that the angle parameter tanθA can be formulated as a function of the product of electrical resistivity and anomalous Hall conductivity. Our scheme was utilized to demonstrate the modulation of tanθA up to a magnitude of 0.46, corresponding to an angle of around 25°. Microfabricated anomalous Hall devices using Fe-doped Co3Sn2S2 single-crystalline nanoflakes exhibit a high Hall sensitivity of 7028 μΩucm/T and a magnetic field detectability of 23.5 nT/Hz0.5 at 1 Hz.
summary: This work reports on methods to significantly enhance the anomalous Hall angle ($	heta_A$) in the magnetic Weyl semimetal $	ext{Co}_3	ext{Sn}_2	ext{S}_2$. By manipulating the material's resistivity and anomalous Hall conductivity through doping or temperature changes, they achieved a large, tunable $	an	heta_A$ of up to 0.46. This breakthrough enables the fabrication of highly sensitive magnetic field detectors for spintronic applications.
main_problem: The primary goal is to enhance the sensitivity of anomalous Hall sensors by modulating the anomalous Hall angle ($	heta_A$), which measures current conversion efficiency.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated modulation of $	an	heta_A$ up to a magnitude of 0.46 (an angle of $\approx 25^\circ$) in the magnetic Weyl semimetal $	ext{Co}_3	ext{Sn}_2	ext{S}_2$.
method: The modulation is achieved by controlling the relationship between anomalous Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{AH}$) and longitudinal resistivity ($ho_{xx}$), using techniques like chemical doping or temperature variation.
model_or_system: The study focuses on $	ext{Co}_3	ext{Sn}_2	ext{S}_2$, a magnetic topological semimetal. The theoretical framework relates $	an	heta_A$ to the product of $ho_{xx}$ and $\sigma_{AH}$, allowing for systematic tuning via doping or structural changes.
key_observables: Anomalous Hall angle ($	heta_A$), anomalous Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{AH}$), longitudinal resistivity ($ho_{xx}$), and magnetic field detectability ($23.5 	ext{ nT}/	ext{Hz}^{0.5}$).
important_parameters: The maximum modulation magnitude of $	an	heta_A$ (up to 0.46) is crucial, as it significantly surpasses the low angles typically found in magnetic materials.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that independent control over both $ho_{xx}$ and $\sigma_{AH}$ can be achieved through different experimental means (e.g., doping for one, temperature/thickness for the other).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of $	an	heta_A$ on varying parameters like temperature or thickness, demonstrating how increasing $ho_{xx}$ and $\sigma_{AH}$ simultaneously enhances the angle.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical problem (enhancing AHE sensitivity), develops a theoretical formulation linking $	an	heta_A$ to transport coefficients ($\sigma_{AH}, ho_{xx}$), presents experimental evidence showing modulation via doping/temperature, and concludes with high-performance sensor metrics.
why_interesting: While primarily condensed matter physics, the precise control over electronic transport coefficients in topological materials using external stimuli (doping, temperature) is relevant to understanding engineered quantum states and boundary effects that underpin many advanced quantum devices.
